parts.label: Roof hinge test
parts.orientation_note: Supplied production-faithful vertical hinge-axis pose. No supports in functional gaps; retain previous tested recipe. Keep supplied vertical hinge-axis pose, preserving the relative positions of both captive bodies. Three knuckle/support starts at Z10, 13 and 30 have reaches 1.4, 1.7 and 1.4 mm. These are short functional ring/attachment ledges, not a large continuous roof ceiling. Keep supports out of bore and captive gaps. Do not chamfer this coupon alone: any underside relief must first be applied identically to the production hinge and rechecked for rotation/clearance.

parts.label: Rear wall-bar test
parts.orientation_note: Supplied reversed vertical rod-axis pose. Existing accessible build-plate-only removable support under fixed bar start. Keep current reversed vertical rod-axis pose and the existing bed-only removable support beneath the accessible 1.8 mm ledge at Z1.5. It has 10.44 mm² horizontal underside. Laying the broad wall face down roughly doubles contact but increases steep downward area 11.24→86.34 mm² and makes the functional rod horizontal. No independent coupon geometry change.

parts.label: Rear snap test
parts.orientation_note: Supplied production-faithful vertical hinge-axis pose. Production roof review retained the joint geometry and vertical hinge-axis pose. Keep bore/lip unsupported; physically test the4.11mm free-ring start with the matching coupon. Existing successful slicing alone is not proof of the surface quality at this start.. Keep supplied vertical-axis calibration pose unless the production roof print pose changes. This is the highest-priority layer-preview point in scope: the C-ring begins at Z3 with two underside patches totaling 6.035 mm² and a 4.1102 mm maximum reach to the immediate lower section. Existing successful no-support slicing alone does not prove this free lip will print cleanly. Roof-face-down (R_y(+90 degrees), supplied -X becomes +Z) is geometrically easier: bed contact 41.845→371.800 mm², horizontal underside 6.035→0, steep downward area 6.035→2.814 mm². However its hinge axis becomes horizontal and its layer direction no longer matches the production roof, so do not change only the calibration coupon. Root print audit should resolve any production start relief/support consistently; preserve bore and spring lip fit.

parts.label: Front anchor test
parts.orientation_note: Upright on16×14mm base, as supplied. No supports in functional gaps; retain previous tested recipe. Keep upright on its 16 × 14 mm base. No above-bed horizontal undersides or surfaces steeper than 45 degrees were detected. Existing barb withdrawal ramps already avoid flat shoulders. Preserve the flex slot; no geometry, orientation or support change recommended.

parts.label: Front socket test
parts.orientation_note: Inside face down, as supplied and matching production front. No supports in functional gaps; retain previous tested recipe. Keep supplied inside-face-down pose, matching the production front. There are no exactly horizontal downward faces, but the arched blind socket ceiling contributes 56.931 mm² of >45-degree downward surface: zero horizontal-face area is not a support-free guarantee. Keep internal support out so it cannot obstruct the fit. Other orientations reduce this metric (blind-end-down reaches 4.73 mm²) but change the ceiling/layer relationship from the production front. No isolated coupon chamfer, teardrop conversion or rotation recommended.
